status_legend.fresh: computed for this review from frozen ledgers or canonical records; scripts in reviews/opus/tools

findings.passage: Opening offers that would complete only the proposer's group are rejected more often than offers that complete nobody (74\% against 64\%); the gap is positive in all five seed blocks and for each of the three systems responding under the standard condition.
findings.finding: The comparator mixes 176 'neither' openings that request a deed with 62 that request none (mostly sell offers, rejected 47/62). A completion request always asks for a deed. Composition-matched: 138/187 (73.8%) vs 105/176 (59.7%), +14.1 points; positive in all five blocks (27.9, 17.8, 10.1, 11.6, 14.3) and for all four recipients including Opus (3/18 vs 2/16). Later offers: 21/102 vs 20/108 (no contrast).
findings.evidence: fresh: tools/cross_checks.py -> data/cross_checks.json A_rejection_composition (two agreeing 920-row ledgers)
findings.resolution: Lead with the matched comparator and report the later-offer null; keep the all-neither figure in the appendix table. Replacement: replacement_prose.tex sec:defence and Table tab:matched.

findings.passage: Responses also do not change with the proposer's post-trade building cash, the quantity agents cite most.
findings.finding: The flat 75/76/55% profile pools across holder cash. Among liquid (>=$300) non-Opus holders rejection rises with the rival's post-trade building cash: 7/10 (no house), 21/29 (one house), 89/110 (full layer). Weak and confounded, but not flat; the smallest original cell (6/11) already ran the other way.
findings.evidence: fresh: data/cross_checks.json C_holder_cash_by_rival_capacity
findings.resolution: Withdraw from abstract, introduction, Section 4.4, Discussion 'Attention without calibration', and conclusion. No categorical-rule mechanism. Optional appendix table, labelled exploratory.

findings.passage: A coherent reading is that the agents apply a categorical rule, roughly ``do not hand a rival a monopoly cheaply'', and then bargain over price with a generic routine.
findings.finding: Mechanism claim rests on OPX-02's cut and on generic counters; the response is graded at least in the holder's own cash (Section 3.9 of review) and weakly in rival capacity. Root reached the same conclusion independently.
findings.evidence: fresh (OPX-02) + root provisional review finding 1
findings.resolution: Delete; replace with the guard-plus-liquidity account (replacement_prose.tex sec:discussion).

findings.passage: its bargaining is not defensive and is reported separately.
findings.finding: Opus counters 141/189 offers; rejection is the wrong measure of its defence. Against the matched comparator its opening ordering is positive (3/18 vs 2/16); its unmortgaged asks are 2.00 to completing vs 1.50 to other buyers. What is distinctive is below-list distress sales (median 0.66x list, n=8) under action-only recovery.
findings.evidence: fresh (matched comparator) + Fable PriceRows/settlement facts (reproduced from frozen ledger)
findings.resolution: Replace with: Opus rarely rejects; it counters, asks more of completing buyers, and supplies most below-list distress sales; model and condition are inseparable.

findings.passage: \subsection{Asking prices rise, bids do not}
findings.finding: Bids differ in sign by system (Sol higher for own completion, Grok lower, Gemini lacks a comparison). 'Holders price a rival's completion more consistently than buyers price their own' flattens heterogeneity.
findings.evidence: inherited/reproduced cells in Opus, Sol, Fable price tables; root finding 3
findings.resolution: Use Sol's formulation: buyer ordering changes across configurations and cuts.

findings.passage: \subsection{A market that clears under distress}
findings.finding: Distress figures condition on settled sales (selected population); 8 of the 14 distressed cash-for-deed completing sales come from Opus under recovery.
findings.evidence: Opus draft distress.json; Fable settlement facts
findings.resolution: Rephrase as composition of observed completing sales; no clearing mechanism.

findings.passage: \title{LLM Agents Withhold a Rival's Monopoly\\Until They Need the Cash
findings.finding: 'Until' is not warranted. At openings, standard-condition holders refuse completion requests 17-21 points more than comparable deed requests in every cash band (<$100: 13/20 vs 4/9; $100-299: 17/24 vs 7/13; >=$300: 105/125 vs 92/138). Gemini rejects 10/10 completion openings under $100; Opus never guards by refusal.
findings.evidence: fresh: tools/liquidity_openings.py -> data/liquidity_openings.json
findings.resolution: Retitle: 'Withholding a Rival's Monopoly: Defensive Bargaining and Liquidity among LLM Agents in Monopoly' (integration_proposal.md).

findings.passage: These deeds move when the holder is short of cash. Holders with under \$100 reject \fact{d.gap.low.pct}\% of the same requests, a gap present in all five seed blocks.
findings.finding: 17/69 vs 120/175 mixes stage (43 of 69 low-cash requests are later offers, rejected 9.3%), recipient (21 to Opus, 0 rejected) and a general liquidity shift (other deed requests 5/22 vs 109/224). Sol's 26 low-cash requests come from 9 threads (root join).
findings.evidence: fresh: data/cross_checks.json B_holder_cash; data/liquidity_openings.json; root fable_comparison.json
findings.resolution: Primary display: opening x cash band x request type, standard-condition holders (Table tab:liquidity in replacement_prose.tex). Phrase as 'cash need makes the guard negotiable'.

findings.passage: What the cash becomes then separates the trajectories.
findings.finding: Seller build/win split (9/14 vs 1/29 sales; 8/13 vs 1/21 player-games) conditions on future behaviour and the eventual winner. Restricting to sellers who already held a complete group keeps the split (8/12 vs 0/8 player-games), but 7 of 9 group-holding non-builders had <$100 at the sale: strength and liquidity, not a use-of-proceeds effect, may drive both.
findings.evidence: fresh: data/cross_checks.json E_seller_conversion (Fable rows joined to Opus completion ledger)
findings.resolution: Remove from abstract and title-level claims; keep a descriptive table with player-game counts and the held-group stratum; state the outcome conditioning.

findings.passage: Exposure to opponents was similar, and the first pair collected \fact{d.conv.rpl.ratio} times the rent per opponent landing.
findings.finding: Post hoc two-and-two grouping; rent per landing is largely the rent schedule once built. Behavioural content is first-window construction (33/35 vs 10/28), tied to mortgaged acquisitions (2,4,7,5) and low post-trade cash (Opus $268) plus response conditions.
findings.evidence: Fable ConversionRows (fresh in Fable; values checked against frozen data)
findings.resolution: Report per-system first-window construction with causes in Results; no ratio in abstract.

findings.passage: Forced liquidation is the one financial task every system handled reliably
findings.finding: 'the one' implies negative findings about other financial tasks that the cohort does not measure.
findings.evidence: scope
findings.resolution: 'All four systems paid nearly every payable debt'.

findings.passage: It is the pattern expected if a blocker is a reserve that its holder gives up when cash runs out, and the agents
findings.finding: Within-pair evidence: cash lower at sale in 13/14, but under $100 at the sale in only 8/14 (5/11 non-Opus); several sales at $444-774. Selected on eventual sale; unsettled pairs also drift down (25/38).
findings.evidence: fresh: data/cross_checks.json D_pairs; Fable facts for unsettled pairs
findings.resolution: 'Release followed a fall in cash', not 'when cash runs out'; report under-$100 count.

findings.passage: Buyers also send completion requests where cash is short.
findings.finding: The 24% vs 8% figure includes later counters and Opus. At openings: 26/187 vs 10/176; without Opus 20/169 vs 9/160; same direction for every recipient system. Offers to cash-poor holders are not more generous (median net cash $165 vs $150 at >=$300).
findings.evidence: fresh: data/liquidity_openings.json opening_targeting
findings.resolution: Use the opening version; place under opponent modelling of liquidity (Q2).

findings.passage: They suggest that this behavior is what bargaining under externalities and cash constraints tends to produce
findings.finding: Extrapolates from two theory analogies untested here; in Monopoly the holder itself bears the externality, unlike Jehiel-Moldovanu's non-buyers.
findings.evidence: IDEAS bibliographic record checked (Econometrica 63(6):1321-1335)
findings.resolution: Keep the analogy as interpretation only.

findings.evidence: Fable handoff

findings.passage: A second finding concerns \emph{executed multi-step reasoning}.
findings.finding: Payment proves executed financing through a scaffolded menu (amount owed, shortfall, legal options supplied), not an observed reasoning process. More informative: 2/68 building-sale payments when mortgages sufficed (Fable), 19 paid episodes using unlocked collateral, and both standard payable eliminations omitting unlocked collateral in a static first-menu sum.
findings.evidence: fresh: tools/unlock_check.py -> data/unlock_check.json; canonical G12 d190, G17 d234 notes read directly
findings.resolution: 'Successful multistep financing'; add the static-lookahead contrast (replacement_prose.tex sec:finance).

findings.passage: Three findings organize the paper. First, bargaining responds to what an exchange enables for another player.
findings.finding: Astra's population bargaining evidence uses author-only vs recipient-only, which changes both who completes and who gives a deed; matched comparator is stronger (OPX-01). Liquidity is absent from the centre.
findings.evidence: fresh (OPX-01, FAB-02)
findings.resolution: Adopt matched comparator and liquidity qualifier.

findings.passage: Among the 131 demonstrably payable episodes, three end in elimination, or 2.3\%.
findings.finding: Census closes identically across three ledgers (188 keys; 128/60; 269 paying actions; 0 fallbacks; one Grok content/call disagreement at G1 d471; all 82 Opus paying decisions under action-only recovery). 131 is an ex post feasibility denominator, not difficulty.
findings.evidence: fresh: data/cross_checks.json G_debt; canonical decisions.jsonl
findings.resolution: Keep 128/131 with its construction stated; report the G1 d471 channel note and Opus condition once.

findings.passage: The three payable eliminations are two miscalculations and one conflict.
findings.finding: Verified from canonical prompts: G12 Sol d190 ($53+$225+$130=$408 vs $500) and G17 Gemini d234 ($500+$30=$530 vs $550) both omit mortgages unlocked by selling buildings ($340, $375). 19 paid episodes executed exactly that step. G17's estate went to the last-placed player, who won. Only Fable states this; it should be central to the planning evidence.
findings.evidence: fresh: canonical decisions read; data/unlock_check.json
findings.resolution: Promote to the finance subsection as a static-lookahead failure contrasted with incremental success (replacement_prose.tex sec:finance).

findings.passage: That reading matches the controlled two-party finding that LLM negotiators can model a counterparty accurately while their final prices follow opening anchors and local adjustment

findings.evidence: read: archived FinBoardBench v1 text (abstract, 3.1-3.2); arXiv abstract page of 2605.16575v1
findings.resolution: Replacement related-work paragraph (replacement_prose.tex sec:related).
